data.description:
## Problem

Every one of the **15** tests in `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` fails on the Windows
advisory sweep with `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file
specified`. The file exercises `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` by invoking it as a shell
script; Windows runners have no such interpreter on PATH, so the subprocess launch fails
before any assertion is reached.

The module carries **no** platform guard. `grep -nE "skipif|os.name|platform|sys.platform"
tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` returns nothing.

## Evidence

Sweep run `35572919806`, job `106248614492` (`sweep (windows)`) at `1b3bf5ffd1f`:

```
$ grep -c "FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py" win.log
15
$ grep -c "^def test_" tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py
15
```

15 of 15. Sample failures:

```
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_with_dir_lock_uses_python_fcntl_when_flock_binary_unavailable - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_with_dir_lock_serializes_concurrent_holders - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_clean_code_workspace_behind_origin_main_fast_forwards - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
```

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

These are not 15 distinct defects. They are one environmental precondition reported 15 times,
and they inflate the Windows failure count without carrying any signal — the same erosion
`6798-606d-...` describes at the whole-lane level. A skip carries the true information ("this
suite requires a POSIX shell") where a failure asserts something false ("the entrypoint is
broken").

The class is also **growing**. `5967-b043-0a4e-4971`'s fix added 2 tests to this module
(`test_with_dir_lock_uses_python_fcntl_when_flock_binary_unavailable` and
`test_with_dir_lock_reports_unavailable_mechanism_not_timeout`), which immediately joined the
failing set. Any future work on the entrypoint enlarges it further, so the guard should land
before the next addition rather than after.

## Suggested direction, to be confirmed by investigation

A module-level skip keyed on the **absence of a POSIX shell** rather than on `os.name` — the
condition that actually matters, and portable to any host lacking one rather than special-casing
a platform. Confirm the real cause is interpreter absence rather than a path-translation issue
before implementing; the WinError 2 could in principle come from the script path rather than the
shell.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause is confirmed by evidence, not assumed: establish that WinError 2 originates from the missing shell interpreter and not from script path translation, and record how that was determined.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` skips, rather than fails, when no POSIX shell is available.
- [ ] The guard keys on the capability (shell availability), not on `os.name`/`sys.platform`, so it remains correct on any host lacking a shell.
- [ ] The skip reason names the missing capability, so a reader of the sweep log learns why without opening the source.
- [ ] All 15 tests still run and pass on Linux and macOS — verified by `make verify` showing no change in that module's results.
- [ ] A Windows sweep after this lands reports 0 failures from `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` and 15 skips.
data.title: All 15 tests in test_mcp_entrypoint.py fail on Windows for want of a shell, with no skip guard
